correctness.rationale: For a strongly nil-clean residue matrix, the commuting idempotent yields generalized 1- and 0-primary blocks. Conversely the coprime primary decomposition constructs the commuting idempotent. The dual coefficient is unrestricted because the relevant Sylvester operator between the two primary blocks is invertible over every field. For fixed primary dimension r, there are {n\brack r}_q q^{r(n-r)} ordered decompositions, q^{r^2-r} and q^{(n-r)^2-(n-r)} nilpotent block choices, and q^{n^2} dual coefficients, giving the stated exponent. Exhaustive checks at (q,n)=(2,1),(2,2),(2,3),(3,1),(3,2),(5,2) return CHECK_OK.
